solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wild Africa's not caught on trek

indicators.note: wild suggests letters running loose into a new order
not tells us to leave the following letter out of the word before it

parts.note: the possessive's S is counted here as a letter of the fodder
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A trekker observes that untamed Africa holds no catches on the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not caught' drops C from AFRICAS, leaving AFRIAS, which 'Wild' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An expedition overland, especially to watch wildlife, is a trek of this kind.

clue.text: Triallist herding Herdwicks?

parts.note: a working collie competes in trials, rounding up flocks such as the Herdwick breed

explanation.walkthrough: Herdwicks are a hardy sheep breed from the English Lake District; sheepdog trials are competitions in herding them.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie entered in herding trials is a triallist whose job is moving a flock.

clue.text: Interminable deluge — call for lino, maybe

indicators.note: interminable, read as without its end, says the last letter goes

parts.note: a deluge is a flood
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A never-ending downpour prompts a call for new lino.
explanation.definitionFit: Lino is one example of a floor covering, so the definition works by example.

clue.text: Worn casing of knife exchanged

indicators.note: the casing of the word is its outer pair of letters, the ones swapped
exchanged says the two outside letters trade places

parts.note: a dagger is a kind of knife

explanation.surface: A knife sheath that has been swapped out because it was worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casing of knife exchanged': the outer letters D and R of DAGGER swap ends, giving RAGGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are tattered and threadbare are worn, the same adjectival sense.

clue.text: Throw up by leading political campaigner

parts.note: to lob is to throw something high
taken as written
1st, written IST, means first or leading

explanation.surface: A political activist throws something by way of protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lobs lobbies MPs is a campaigner who tries to sway legislators.

clue.text: Some school's out up in capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the run is read from the bottom upwards
some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run lying across them

explanation.surface: Some schools are out for the holidays up in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes OLSO from schOOL'S Out, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian capital city, a straightforward example of a capital.

clue.text: Catcalls heard at successes for benders

indicators.note: heard means we want what the word sounds like when spoken

parts.note: boos are jeering catcalls
ups, as in ups and downs, are successes

explanation.surface: Jeers ring out at a series of triumphs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns BOOS into BOOZE; 'at' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bender is slang for a heavy drinking session, a drunken spree.

clue.text: Dictator books small chumps

parts.note: Idi Amin was the Ugandan dictator
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A tyrant reserves a few chumps for himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Chumps and fools are both terms for foolish people, synonyms in the plural.

clue.text: Almost top ancient city

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the very best is the top, the finest

explanation.surface: An ancient city was nearly the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of ancient Egypt and also a city of ancient Greece.

clue.text: One hug should prove sufficient

indicators.note: should prove suggests the letters will turn out to form something else

explanation.surface: A single embrace ought to be enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough as an adjective means as much as is needed, a synonym.

clue.text: Mineral took to the air okay, Cockney said

indicators.note: Cockney said means the phrase as a Cockney speaker would pronounce it

parts.note: took to the air is flew; okay is all right, a Cockney orright

explanation.surface: A Londoner reports that the flight went fine.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney accent turns 'flew all right' into something like 'flew-orrite'; Cockney is the working-class London accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluorspar, calcium fluoride, is a well-known crystalline mineral.

clue.text: Frivolity. Yes! Having sang out!

indicators.note: out signals the letters set out in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A cheerful cry after someone has had a good sing.
explanation.definitionFit: In the older sense, being merry and light-hearted is frivolity.

clue.text: Me, not I, in capital with an Italian cheese

indicators.note: Me not I means one replaces the other

parts.note: Paris is the French capital
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eating an Italian cheese in Paris insists it is them, not the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me, not I' is a swap instruction: 'not' marks the letter being replaced in the capital, and the surface's first person is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard grating cheese from Parma is a famous Italian cheese.

clue.text: Get comfortable and pay the bill

definitions.meaning: to ... down into a chair is to get comfortable
to ... an account is to pay it

explanation.surface: A diner relaxes and then pays for the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard verb senses: to settle into a seat and to settle up a debt.

clue.text: More tipsy right after German's England

indicators.note: after puts the second piece following the first

parts.note: Merrie England is a light opera by Edward German

explanation.surface: A drunker man, a German in England, sits to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward German was an English composer whose 1902 comic opera is called 'Merrie England'.
explanation.definitionFit: Merry is a mild word for tipsy, so its comparative means more drunk.

clue.text: Has snow melted?

indicators.note: melted suggests the word losing its shape and re-forming

explanation.surface: A question about whether the snow has thawed.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, so this is a synonym of has.

clue.text: Rough on the seabed, holding nothing, containers missing

indicators.note: the containers are the outermost letters, and missing means they go

parts.note: something sunk lies on the seabed
something holding nothing is empty

explanation.surface: Wreck debris lies on the ocean floor, empty, its cargo boxes lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containers missing' strips the very first and last letters off the two joined synonyms; the surface's lost cargo boxes are a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt hair or appearance is untidy and rough-looking.

clue.text: Goodbye. Can I move to city in Spain?

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

indicators.note: move asks for the letters to be shifted around

explanation.surface: Bidding farewell, someone asks to relocate to a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: VALE is the Latin farewell; 'move' rearranges CAN I into NCIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain's third-largest city, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Baronet admits need for necromancy

indicators.note: admits means the first word lets the second inside it

parts.note: Bart is an abbreviation for baronet
lack means need or want

explanation.surface: A titled man confesses his dependency on sorcery.
explanation.definitionFit: Black magic, including communing with the dead, is the dark art in question.

clue.text: Carer having seat on May Day!

parts.note: a seat can be a home, as in a country seat
Mayday is the radio distress call, a call for help

explanation.surface: A carer gets to sit down on the first of May.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayday is the international distress signal, a cry for HELP.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic assistant who looks after someone at home is a carer.

clue.text: Break in line may be cause of rail accidents, initially

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else
initially takes the first letters of rail and accidents

explanation.surface: A broken track could be what leads to railway crashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives R and A, which join CAUSE to be rearranged under 'may be'.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry a caesura is a pause or break within a line of verse.

clue.text: Chorister in Walton's embrace

indicators.note: the word embraces the required letters within it

explanation.surface: A choir singer is held in the composer Walton's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer of the lowest female or highest male choral part is a chorister.

clue.text: Sheltered, quiet, dead worried

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet

indicators.note: worried suggests the letters being shaken about

explanation.surface: Someone protected and quiet is deeply anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaded from the sun means protected or sheltered from it.

clue.text: Insulting emails from your exes!

definitions.meaning: abusive online messages are known as these
former lovers are old ones of these

explanation.surface: Rude emails sent by former partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Online abuse is called this, and old lovers are called old ones.

clue.text: Ward off consuming last bit of dinner — and suffer thus?

indicators.note: consuming means the first word takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: to stave off is to ward off

indicators.note: last bit of means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fending off food leaves one going hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts R, the last letter of dinner, inside STAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without food, as by warding off dinner, is to suffer hunger.

clue.text: Noddy greeting lord and queen

parts.note: ho, as in what ho, is a greeting
ER is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A nodding figure greets a lord and a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Noddy Holder was lead singer of the 1970s British rock band Slade.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename identifies a famous rock singer by his surname.

clue.text: Charm for small festival made out of lace

parts.note: Pent is short for Pentecost, the festival

indicators.note: made out of suggests the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A lucky charm crafted from lace for a little fair.
explanation.walkthrough: Pent. abbreviates Pentecost; 'made out of' rearranges LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentacle is a five-pointed star used as a magic talisman.

clue.text: Where to cook the joint right away

indicators.note: away means the letter is removed

parts.note: a roast is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: Directions on where to put the meat in the oven immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a kiln for drying hops; 'right away' looks like immediately but it removes R.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln, so loosely a place for heating or cooking.

clue.text: Politician at public protest with heartless European

parts.note: a demo is a public demonstration

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter goes

parts.note: a Croat is a European from Croatia

explanation.surface: A politician at a demonstration alongside an unfeeling European.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Democratic Party, chiefly in the US, is a politician.

clue.text: Establish academy in island setting

indicators.note: setting means the island forms a frame around the next piece

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island
A is an abbreviation for academy, as in RA, the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: An academy is founded on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something up is to establish it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Top lines of the French anthems — not hard

parts.note: des is French for of the

indicators.note: not tells us to omit the next letter

parts.note: chants are sung anthems
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: The opening lines of French anthems are soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Descants are melodies sung above the main tune, so the top lines.

clue.text: "Clunk, Click — and do stop talking!"

definitions.meaning: a British road-safety slogan urging drivers to fasten their seatbelt
a rude instruction to shut up

explanation.surface: A driver fastening up while telling a passenger to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Clunk Click was a 1970s UK seatbelt campaign slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both fasten a seatbelt and be quiet, two idioms.
